existing_capabilities.capacity: Detects GoNet/GoAzimut markers then extracts PV document links from robots-allowed municipal HTML; it does not render a portal DOM.
Reads the public VPlus API route tree and page details, then retains only real PV-labelled vplus-documents PDFs; no Chromium.
Uses the server-rendered RSS feed and embedded Wix JSON to emit real CDN PDF pairs for the shared DOM deposit gate.
Queries /wp-json/wp/v2/media and accepts only live PV-labelled document media.
Follows the living host, canonical PV paths and sitemaps, then uses the shared structural parser for static WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and plain HTML pages.
Launches one Chromium CDP browser, obtains document.documentElement.outerHTML after JavaScript, follows rendered PV navigation and canonical paths, then applies the existing PV quality gate.

Accepts a DOM or anchor pairs already obtained after Playwright interaction (accordion, year selector, shadow DOM or ASP postback), reuses the obscura parser, and live-checks the resulting real links.
The zones lane already has a CDP browser that returns rendered DOM and observed network requests, and can keep an authenticated session for an in-page fetch.
Recognises gestionweblex and ASP.NET runtime-injected indexes and routes them to a browser rather than treating an empty static parse as absence.

capture_compliance_gap.finding: The existing PV speciality runners are discovery/index-manifest tools, not a deployable captured CDP source today. Several use direct source fetches; the current capture job is explicitly direct HTTP only.
capture_compliance_gap.consequence: No existing runner may be launched unchanged for a new probe under the current capturedFetch-only rule; this is a deployment/provenance integration gap, not evidence that a new editor adapter is needed.

portal_sample.classification_rule: The survey stored status, URL, size and SHA-256 evidence, but not the DOM body. Publisher-specific markers therefore cannot be reconstructed for eleven cases without a new captured probe, which this report does not perform.

confirmed_specific_host_family_matches.note: This proves a matching existing route, not that its API or page will yield a PV; no such runner was launched.

conditional_url_shape_matches.note: These route signatures are insufficient to assert the publisher without retained DOM bytes.

existing_adapter_confrontation.interpretation: All 18 are valid inputs to the existing generic PV CDP renderer because each returned HTML 200; 17 also exposed a PV-designating page. This is eligibility, not a claimed extraction success. A per-editor adapter is premature until a captured rendered-DOM result classifies the eleven unknown publishers and any interaction/WAF failure.

portal_only_b.meaning: Additional municipalities in the b portal/JS/anti-bot partition if that sample proportion held.

a_b_c_potentially_reachable.meaning: Total a+b+c potential; it includes the 37.0 expected a cases already reachable as direct PDFs, so it is not the incremental portal-only lever.

could_be_false_if: the random n=30 does not represent MRC, municipality size, hosts or publishers of the 222
the unclassified portal distribution differs from the sample
WAF or interactive-session requirements dominate after real rendering
a rendered portal lists no retrievable PV despite its navigation page

proposal.smallest_increment: Do not build an editor-specific adapter first. Capitalise the existing PV CDP renderer as a captured source in a separate obscura image/worklist variant: browser navigation and every discovered document request must cross capturedFetch, then use the already-existing parser and DOM handoff for interaction-only cases.
proposal.why: One generic renderer accepts all 18 current HTML-200 cases; eleven have no retained publisher fingerprint, so a family-first adapter choice would be speculative.
proposal.implementation_cost_not_asserted: No line-count or duration estimate is claimed: the repo contains the rendering and parsing logic, but not a capture-compliant PV CDP deployment path.
